references.text: The Lord saw the suffering of the Israelites in Egypt and brought them out, as Gideon refers to when he mentions that the Lord brought them up from Egypt.
Israel's complaint at the Red Sea resembles Gideon's question about where the Lord's miraculous deeds have gone.
The command to tell the children about the exodus from Egypt, which Gideon alludes to when he says that the fathers told of the Lord's mighty works.
The psalmist remembers how the fathers told of God's powerful deeds in times past, similar to Gideon's reference to the testimony of the fathers.
Asaph's complaint that the Lord seems to have abandoned his people and the question of whether he has forgotten his miraculous deeds.
The passing down of God's works from the fathers to the children, as Gideon notes that the fathers told of the miracles.
Israel's remembrance of the days of old when the Lord brought them up from Egypt with his mighty arm.
Moses' prophecy that the people will say that evils come upon them because God is not among them, similar to Gideon's doubt about the Lord's presence.
